# 🚧 What it cannot see, and what the tests do not prove

The limits of [the coverage report](agents.md), kept beside it rather than in it.
Generated from `docs/blind-spots.yaml` and each scenario's `known_gaps`; lint fails
when it drifts.

## What osquery cannot see

These are properties of the platform and the tables, not of any one scenario, so
they are stated once. No amount of test coverage moves them.

| blind spot | why |
|---|---|
| Anything inside a VM, a Codespace or a cloud dev box | The scanner sees the machine it runs on. Containers are the exception and only partly: `--deep` reads images, running containers and their vendor labels, so an agent IN a container is now visible from outside it |
| What a process inside a container is doing | `docker_containers` gives the container's own command and entrypoint, which is what it was started as. The processes actually running inside it are in `docker_container_processes`, which requires a constraint on the container id -- reachable through a join, verified -- and is not collected, because a cmdline can carry `--api-key` and redaction is not designed yet |
| A container that is not running | `docker_containers` lists RUNNING containers only. Measured 2026-09-11 on Docker 28.4.0: two exited containers produced zero rows. A stopped agent container is seen through its image and not as a container, so an empty container list is not an empty machine |
| Containers outside Docker Desktop, and Podman anywhere | Colima, Rancher Desktop and Podman keep their sockets elsewhere, and `docker_images` cannot read containerd or Podman image stores. Podman's socket is deliberately not probed: it would pass the health check and return zero images, which reads as "we looked". The runtime is NAMED instead: `bin/container-scan` looks for a socket or a binary on disk -- presence only, no daemon conversation -- and the marker row reads `unreadable:podman` rather than `absent`, which is the word a machine with no containers gets. What is still unknown is whether it holds any containers at all, and what they are |
| Whether an image is really the vendor's, when the vendor sets no label | An image name is chosen by whoever tags it, so `docker tag alpine paulgauthier/aider` produces the same finding. The `image_labels` route closes this for vendors who set `org.opencontainers.image.source`, which a retagger cannot forge -- but that is a fact about a project's release pipeline, not about being an agent. Measured 2026-09-11: the currently published ghcr.io/openhands/openhands and ghcr.io/block/goose carry it; paulgauthier/aider carries no labels at all and sweagent/swe-agent only its base image's, so for those two a finding is exactly as forgeable as the tag |
| An untagged (dangling) image | Untested -- no dangling image existed on the machine this was measured on. Unknown, not covered |
| Snap and Flatpak packages | osquery has no `snap_packages` or `flatpak_packages` table at any version, checked against the source at 5.10.0 and 5.23.1. A snap- or flatpak-installed agent is invisible on every package route |
| Alpine Linux, and apk packages anywhere | Two walls, and either alone would do. osquery has no `apk_packages` table at any version: absent from the published schemas for 4.5.0, 5.0.1 and 5.23.1, and `SELECT count(*) FROM apk_packages` answers `no such table` on Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora 41 at 5.23.1. And osquery ships no musl build: its 5.23.1 Linux tarball, the only non-deb, non-rpm artifact, fails to load on alpine:3.22 even with gcompat and libstdc++ installed (`Error relocating osqueryd: __res_init: symbol not found`, then argz_*, canonicalize_file_name and nine more). Measured 2026-10-20. So an Alpine host cannot run the collector, and an agent installed from an apk repository -- Claude Code publishes one -- is invisible on every route, not only the package ones |
| AppImage and tarball installs on Linux | Neither leaves a package record, and Cursor's primary Linux download is an AppImage. Only `desktop_ids` can see one, and only if the install writes a `.desktop` entry |
| A binary installed under /usr/local/bin | `binaries` is a `~/`-rooted route and the enumeration reads ~/.local/bin, so a vendor installer or pkg that writes to /usr/local/bin leaves nothing any route reads. Muse Code's muse.pkg does exactly that: its whole payload is /usr/local/bin/muse, read off the expanded package on 2026-10-19. Its curl installer, which is the route the vendor documents, writes ~/.local/bin/muse and is covered |
| An NSS-only account whose home directory is outside /home or /root | Since osquery 5.13.1 the unconstrained Linux `users` table reads /etc/passwd directly, so an account that only an NSS module knows -- GCE OS Login, SSSD, LDAP, Active Directory -- is not in it. The browser and VS Code branches take their uids from the home directories on disk as well, which covers every such account that has logged in under /home or /root. One whose home was placed elsewhere, or one that has never logged in, is reached by neither list. Read off osquery's linux/users.cpp at 5.23.1 |
| Which agent installed a systemd unit | No unit name is a signature. The macOS launchd prefixes were read off live installs; no Linux unit name has been, so the route carries no values and unit rows stay evidence |
| A systemd unit the running manager has not loaded | `systemd_units` lists loaded units, not unit files on disk -- unlike macOS's `launchd`. So a unit installed but never started is invisible, and so is anything under `systemctl --user`, which reads a different bus |
| Windows, entirely | No queries, no routes, no runner. It is a parallel PowerShell implementation rather than a port: `bin/` is bash and every scenario is a shell script |
| Which filesystem roots an MCP server exposes | Requires parsing arbitrary JSON config; osquery has no table for it |
| Outbound destinations by hostname | `process_open_sockets` returns an IP, not a name |
| Which agent holds a listening port | A port is only attributable when the process holding it already names the agent, so it never identifies anything on its own -- 8080-held-by-java would read as llama.cpp. Ports are collected as evidence and are never a signature |
| A cloned-but-never-run source checkout | Nothing has been created on disk yet |
| What an agent *does* | Every route reports presence and declared capability. `permissions` says an extension **may** read every page, never that it did |
| The identity of a sideloaded extension | osquery derives `identifier` from the manifest `key`, which unpacked and sideloaded extensions do not carry, so they report an empty one. A Web Store CRX does carry it. The row is not anonymous: it carries `unreferenced` when Chrome would not load it, or `sideloaded:` and the manifest's SHA-256 when it would, so a sideload is found by hash rather than by id |
| GitHub Copilot inside VS Code | Copilot Chat now ships BUILT IN: VS Code's own bundle carries `GitHub.copilot-chat` 0.64.1 among its 97 built-in extensions, and `vscode_extensions` reports only the user extension directories -- a run with 97 built-ins present returned 2 rows, both user-installed. The marketplace `github.copilot` cannot be installed over it either, because it pins `github.copilot-chat` 0.48.1 and VS Code refuses to downgrade a built-in, so no scenario can produce the identifier. Measured on VS Code stable, 2026-09-05. The route therefore cannot identify Copilot at all, which is why no signature is carried rather than one that would match every VS Code install -- `copilot-cli` is the Copilot this catalog can prove, through npm, Homebrew and the JetBrains plugin. Detecting the built-in would report the EDITOR, not a fleet's choice of agent |
| VS Code extensions on osquery below 5.11.0 | `vscode_extensions` arrived in 5.11.0, above this repo's 5.10.0 floor, so `queries/vscode.sql` declares its own minimum and returns nothing on an older endpoint. The `vscode_edition` column that tells VS Code from Cursor and Windsurf came in 5.15.0 |
| JetBrains plugins on osquery below 5.18.0 | `jetbrains_plugins` arrived in 5.18.0, so `queries/jetbrains.sql` declares that floor and returns nothing on an older endpoint. The composed artifact is one statement, so on 5.11 to 5.17 it fails whole; `bin/discover --write` runs the branch on its own and reports it as `error` |
| The identity of a JetBrains plugin | The table exposes no plugin.xml id, only a display name, a vendor and the path, so the identifier is the plugin's directory name. A plugin whose directory was renamed on disk is not recognised, and a plugin shipped as a bare jar carries its version in the name |
| Whether an agent was running a minute ago | A `proc` row is a sample of the process table when the query ran, not a history. An agent started and stopped between two runs leaves nothing on this route |
| A running node CLI that names no package path | A global launched through its bin link reads `node /usr/local/bin/<name>`, and a process that renames itself carries no path at all. `queries/running.sql` finds OpenClaw's gateway through its workers, which run a script under node_modules/openclaw; a CLI that starts none is found as installed and not as running |
| Behaviour that only appears after launch or sign-in | Nothing here launches an app -- `open -a` needs an Aqua session and SSH has none -- so first-launch daemons, ports and state directories go unobserved, and account-gated products are never signed in to |
| Whether ChatGPT's dots is enabled or in use | A dot runs on an OpenAI cloud computer; local computer access is opt-in and runs through the ChatGPT desktop app, which `chatgpt-desktop` already reports (help.openai.com/en/articles/20001554-manage-dots-in-chatgpt-workspaces). No dots-only signal has been read off a real install, so a match means the app, never dots |

## What the scenarios do not prove

The install succeeded and the identifier matched. These are the ways it still falls short of the real thing -- each one fixable by work, none of them catchable by a table of counts.

| scenario | not proven |
|---|---|
| 10-desktop-apps, 11-perplexity-desktop | Paid or account-gated in several cases. The install is unattended and the sign-in is not, so nothing exercises behaviour that only appears once a user is signed in. |
| 10-desktop-apps | Kiro CLI is not installed here, though it shares a vendor with kiro: it is a different product, and 21-cli-agents-homebrew installs its cask beside the other CLIs. |
| 12-chatgpt-pre-rename | The bundle id only. A direct download leaves no Homebrew record, so the `chatgpt` brew route is not exercised here; 10-desktop-apps covers it. |
| 13-desktop-apps-more | Trae and Trae CN were read off their dmgs' Info.plist rather than a local install: the VM this was developed in had no IPv4 route to their CDNs. CI is the first real install of both. |
| 13-desktop-apps-more | Sign-in gated, like 10: nothing exercises behaviour that appears once a user signs in. |
| 14-meta-muse | `~/.local/bin/muse` claims the launcher only. muse-bin-<version> beside it is read as unmatched evidence, not as a value: the launcher is always written with it, so the agent is found anyway, and claiming every `muse-<something>` would claim other vendors' tools. |
| 14-meta-muse | Sign-in gated once installed, like 10: Muse for Mac is never launched, so its first-run permission prompts and whatever it writes under ~/Library go unobserved, and Muse Code is never run, so ~/.muse -- which the binary names for projects and worktrees -- is not produced here. |
| 14-meta-muse | The DMG is whatever the production Sparkle channel serves on the day. A build that changes its bundle id shows up as a missing com.meta.endo, which is the point; a build that only bumps the version is recorded as that version. |
| 40-browser | The planted extension is unreferenced by construction, so the sideloaded token is exercised only by 45-claude-extension. |
| 45-claude-extension | Chrome for Testing registers the extension, because branded Chrome 137 and later refuse --load-extension. Branded Chrome's own install, update and ExtensionInstallForcelist paths are untested, and whether the policy needs an MDM-delivered profile on macOS is UNVERIFIED. |
| 55-openclaw-npm | The gateway runs with --allow-unconfigured --auth none, which is not how a real deployment runs it: enough to open the listener and keep the process this scenario asserts running, with no channel connected and no model reachable. |
| 56-openclaw-retired-names | The npm names only. The macOS side of this lineage is 57-clawdbot-era, which installs the Clawdbot-era app and proves its bundle id. |
| 57-clawdbot-era | The bundle id only. com.clawdbot. as a launchd prefix is NOT asserted: the binary contains com.clawdbot.gateway, but a LaunchAgent is registered when the app RUNS and this scenario only installs. Unverified, so not in the catalog either. |
| 57-clawdbot-era | Clawdis, the generation before this one, ships its own macOS app and is not covered. Its bundle id has not been read off the artifact, so nothing is claimed about it. |
| 70-linux-baseline | Runs on whatever base image the job uses, so it proves nothing about a loaded desktop. 00-baseline has the same limitation on macOS. |
| 71-linux-cli-agents | Claude Code's npm identifier is not exercised here -- the native installer is its primary route and the two would fight over the same binary name. 21-cli-agents-homebrew makes the same argument on macOS. |
| 72-linux-python-agents | Whether ~/.hermes appears depends on the install route: the vendor's curl installer creates it, a uv install does not until the agent runs. The run records what appeared rather than asserting it. |
| 73-linux-deb | The AppImage, which is Cursor's primary Linux download, is not installed here. desktop_ids is the route that would catch it, and this scenario exercises that route through the .deb's own entry instead. |
| 74-linux-dpkg-removed | Asserts on a pair of ordinary packages rather than on an agent, because no catalogued agent's deb can be installed and removed without also removing the evidence this checks for. |
| 75-linux-browser | No real extension identifier. 45-claude-extension gets one on macOS by unpacking the Web Store's signed CRX, which does carry the key; the same route would work here and is not yet built. |
| 75-linux-browser | Google ships no Linux arm64 Chrome, so this skips on arm64 runners. |
| 75-linux-browser | The planted extension is unreferenced by construction. The sideloaded token is exercised only on macOS, by 45-claude-extension. |
| 76-linux-systemd | Skips wherever there is no system dbus -- a container has none, which is what the kind=scan marker in queries/runtime-linux.sql exists to report. It runs for real on a GitHub ubuntu runner, where systemd is PID 1, and on every family under test/run-gce.sh and test/run-ec2.sh. |
| 76-linux-systemd | No agent's systemd unit name has been read off a real install, so this proves the query and the matcher and not any vendor's naming. The route is registered and carries no values for exactly that reason. |
| 76-linux-systemd | systemd user units (systemctl --user) are not visible to the table at all, and a per-user agent gateway is exactly the thing that would be one. |
| 77-linux-rpm | Runs in Rocky 9, Fedora 41 and Amazon Linux 2023 containers on an ubuntu runner, because GitHub offers no RPM-distro runner. A container has no systemd, so `unit` is 0 here and the systemd marker reports absent -- correctly. test/run-gce.sh runs it on a Rocky 9 VM and test/run-ec2.sh on Amazon Linux 2023 instances, where it is not. |
| 78-linux-vscode | min-osquery for this branch is 5.11.0, above the 5.10.0 the rest of the repo declares. On a 5.10.x endpoint the query returns [] and exits 1, which is why it is its own pack entry and its own composed branch. |
| 78-linux-vscode | Neither agent's state directory is exercised. ~/.continue does not exist after `code --install-extension` -- verified on a real install -- because it appears on first activation in the editor, and nothing here opens a GUI session. So this proves the extension route and says nothing about the path routes for either. |
| 78-linux-vscode | vscode_edition is reported but not asserted beyond the forbid: this installs into VS Code only, so the cursor, windsurf, vscodium and trae editions the column can report are unexercised. |
| 79-linux-image | A pull proves the registry still serves this repository under this name. It does not prove the image is the vendor's: an image name is chosen by whoever tags it, so `docker tag alpine paulgauthier/aider` produces the same finding. The `image_labels` route is the answer to that for the agents whose vendors set labels, and aider and swe-agent are exactly the ones who do not -- so for those two the finding remains as forgeable as the tag. |
| 79-linux-image | The container probe runs `sleep`, not the agent. It proves the daemon reports a running container from a catalogued image and that the route matches it; it proves nothing about an agent actually working, which would need credentials and a model endpoint this scenario deliberately does not hold. |
| 79-linux-image | Nothing here reads processes inside the container. docker_container_processes requires a constraint on the container id and can be reached through a join, but the cmdline it returns can carry an API key, so it is not collected until redaction is designed. |
| 79-linux-image | swe-agent's `latest` tag was built 2024-12-07, twenty-one months before this scenario was written. The pull proves the registry still serves it; it does not prove anyone still publishes there. |
| 80-linux-jetbrains | The Marketplace zip is unpacked rather than installed by an IDE, so the IDE's own install, update and disable paths are untested, and so is the product directory name an installed IDE writes. |
| 80-linux-jetbrains | The macOS directory, ~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/<Product>/plugins, is not exercised. Only the Linux layout has been read. |
| 81-linux-bun | bun blocks the lifecycle scripts of untrusted packages, and gemini-cli has none. Whether a global that needs its postinstall is still reported after bun skipped it is not proved here. |
| 81-linux-bun | A global directory moved by BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR or bunfig's globalDir is not searched. |
| 81-linux-bun | Packages run through bunx and never installed land in bun's cache, the same gap npx has, noted in queries/filesystem.sql. |
| 82-linux-running | The gateway runs with a throwaway token and no channel or model. This proves what a running gateway looks like to osquery, not an agent at work. |
| 83-linux-claude-running | `claude mcp serve` runs unauthenticated with no client connected, so this proves what a running Claude Code process looks like to osquery, not an agent at work. |
| 83-linux-claude-running | Skips in a default container, where osquery cannot read another user's executable path. It runs for real on CI's ubuntu runner and under test/run-gce.sh and test/run-ec2.sh. |
| 84-linux-installers | Only the installers' Linux branches run here. On macOS opencode, Cursor CLI, goose and Kiro CLI are proved through Homebrew in 21-cli-agents-homebrew, Muse Code by the same installer in 14-meta-muse, and Pi's installer runs in 20-cli-agents; Grok Build's macOS install is unexercised, though ~/.grok is a posix route. |
| 84-linux-installers | Nothing is run after installing, so state that appears on first use -- ~/.config/goose, ~/.local/share/opencode, ~/.muse -- is unexamined. Only the last is a top-level directory the enumeration would reach, and it is not a catalog value. |
| 85-linux-vscode-agents | Installed into VS Code only. Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium and Trae keep their own extension directories, which osquery reports under vscode_edition, and none is exercised. |
| 85-linux-vscode-agents | Blackbox's extensions are unpublished from the Marketplace and arrive here as the VSIX the Marketplace still serves by URL. If that URL stops answering, the two ids can no longer be produced, which is the cue to supersede them rather than drop them. |
| 86-linux-jetbrains-agents | Unpacked from the Marketplace zip, not installed by an IDE, as in 80: the IDE's own install and update paths are untested. |
| 86-linux-jetbrains-agents | Amazon Q's plugin needs AWS Core (aws.toolkit.core) to load in an IDE. It is not installed, because only the directory is under test. |
| 87-linux-pi | Over-matches under bun: OpenClaw 2026.1.29 to 2026.5.27 depended on pi-coding-agent, and `bun add -g` hoists it beside the global, so such a host reports Pi as well. npm -g nests it and is unaffected. Measured with bun 1.4.3. |
| 89-linux-claude-deb | /usr/bin/claude is not a route. binaries is home-rooted, and the package row carries the version, which the binary's path does not, so dpkg's row is the better evidence anyway. |
| 89-linux-claude-deb | Anthropic's apk repository cannot be exercised, and no route could read it: osquery has no apk_packages table at any version, and osquery's own builds are glibc-linked and do not load on musl, so an Alpine host cannot run the collector at all. Measured 2026-10-20 on alpine:3.22; docs/blind-spots.yaml carries it. 91-linux-claude-rpm carries the dnf repository. |
| 91-linux-claude-rpm | Runs in Rocky 9, Fedora 41 and Amazon Linux 2023 containers on an ubuntu runner, because GitHub offers no RPM-distro runner. A container has no systemd, so `unit` is 0 here and the systemd marker reports absent, correctly. |
| 91-linux-claude-rpm | Anthropic's apk repository cannot be exercised, and no route could read it: osquery has no apk_packages table at any version, and osquery's own builds are glibc-linked and do not load on musl, so an Alpine host cannot run the collector at all. Measured 2026-10-20 on alpine:3.22; docs/blind-spots.yaml carries it. |

`14-meta-muse` needs macOS 14 or newer, so CI skips it on older runners rather than failing it. Its `requires.json` carries the reason.

`11-perplexity-desktop`, `50-autonomous`, `57-clawdbot-era` need macOS 15 or newer, so CI skips them on older runners rather than failing them. Each scenario's `requires.json` carries the reason.
